retrospective.harder_than_needed: The story's five properties span very different code shapes (a synchronous dispatcher LRU, an async pending-signal buffer with a marker-aware resolver, a real IDB-backed merge, and a stateful one-shot gate), so each property needed its own from-scratch trace through the real production code (applicationRumorDispatcher.ts, messageEdits/api.ts's ~1550-line module including its buffered/marker resolution paths, chatPersistence.ts's tombstoneMessage re-check, groupStorage.ts's mergeMemberProfile) before a correct, non-guessed test design was possible — in particular, AC-XCUT-4's unauthorized-case ChangeResultKind label legitimately differing between the immediate-known-row path ('discarded') and the buffered-then-resolved path ('noop') had to be traced through resolveKnownRowAgainstStores/applyToKnownSlotCore before writing the assertion, to avoid either a false 'violation' report or a test asserting the wrong invariant (raw kind equality vs. substantive storage-outcome equality).
retrospective.surprised_by: None of the property tests revealed a real production invariant violation — all five whole-flow guarantees held under every constructed ordering, including the deliberately adversarial AC-XCUT-4 competing-pending-signals case (a lower-rev attacker signal buffered concurrently with a higher-rev legitimate one never won, regardless of arrival order) and the AC-XCUT-2 real-storage redelivery case (upsert-by-id never inflated the tally).
